turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I’m having a really hard time keeping things organized. Like, I’m trying to manage schoolwork and also my little accessories shop, and everything just ends up in piles—supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes. I look at it all and I don’t know what I’m supposed to do first.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient reports being unable to organize schoolwork and shop-related supplies, deadlines, receipts, and notes, which accumulate in piles and make prioritization difficult.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks, even when you want to focus?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. Like in class, or if I’m watching a video for one of my business assignments, I’ll start off actually listening and trying to focus. But after a few minutes my mind drifts to charm designs or order ideas, and then I realize I missed a big chunk of what was said.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient reports that despite trying to listen and focus in class or during assignment videos, their mind drifts after a few minutes and they miss substantial content.

turns.doctor_question: Did these focus and organization problems already happen when you were a child?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I think so. My mom still has notes from elementary school where teachers wrote that I was always getting out of my seat, talking before I was called on, and rushing through group activities. It wasn’t that I didn’t understand the work—I just had a hard time slowing down and waiting.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient reports teachers noted that they were always getting out of their seat in elementary school.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient reports talking before being called on, consistent with blurting out before an appropriate turn.
symptom_reasoning.S017: They describe difficulty slowing down and waiting, supporting difficulty waiting their turn.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or wired and needed much less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I can feel restless or have trouble winding down sometimes, but I haven’t noticed a stretch where I barely needed sleep and felt unusually wired like that.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient reports sometimes feeling restless.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient denies a sustained period of feeling unusually energetic or wired.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient denies having a stretch in which they barely needed sleep.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel like your mind is occupied by a lot of worry?

turns.doctor_question: Did these problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful event or change in your life?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I think it got more noticeable after I changed schools. That was about two years ago—maybe a little over two years. I had to manage the business program and my accessories shop with less structure, and that’s when it started feeling like a real problem.

turns.doctor_question: Do these problems ever make it hard for you to manage everyday responsibilities at home?
turns.patient_response: Yes. It’s made it hard to keep up with things I’m supposed to handle. I missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid is at risk. And with my shop projects, people I work with have started relying on me less because I don’t always keep things on track.
